title: Write clear upgrade messages for when free educators reach the Starter plan's limits, by Fri 20 Nov
description: The Starter plan allows up to 3 cohorts with limited AI help, and the moment an educator hits a limit is the best moment to explain Pro, but only if the message is helpful, not pushy. Work under this goal: list every limit and upgrade point on the Starter plan, checked against the live pricing page and app; write the in-app message, button text and follow-up email for each one, explaining in plain words what Pro adds and its price; and write a short FAQ on upgrading, billing and downgrading. Only prices and features confirmed on the live site. Separate from the pricing page usability and cost calculator goals. Done when all messages, emails and the FAQ are delivered and approved by the team.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Show each draft upgrade prompt to five free educators and rewrite from their answers
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Copy that converts gets tested on the people who hit the wall, not written once and shipped. Approach: after the prompts are drafted against verified limits, show each one (text only, in context screenshots) to five real free educators from public communities and record what they'd do next. Rewrite from those answers; anything fifteen words long gets cut. Tasks: five-person check with consent (research), rewrite pass (content).

pendingIdeas.title: Name the plan before writing the upgrade message: one cap, one screen, one verified price
pendingIdeas.description:
What I checked on 22 October 2026: the live pricing page sells the paid plan as "Pro, 20K naira /month" in the plan card, but the comparison table on the same page has columns headed Starter, Growth and Enterprise. The free card says Starter, up to 3 cohorts, up to 5 teachers/admins, limited AI. So an educator who hits a cap and clicks upgrade is sent to a plan the same page calls two different names. Any upgrade message written before that is settled will name the wrong plan at the one moment the user is deciding.

What I propose:

1. Capture the actual cap moments in the app first: the third cohort, the sixth teacher/admin, a student over the per-cohort limit, the limited AI assistant, the second workspace, and the analytics/API limit the table lists. For each, record the screen, the URL and the words already on it. If a cap has no screen, record that - do not invent one.
2. Freeze the plan name and price from the billing screen, not the marketing card, and write it once with its source and check date. Every message then uses that exact name and the price shown at checkout.
3. Write one message per cap in the same shape: what you just hit, what the paid plan changes for this specific cap, the price, and one button. No generic "upgrade to unlock more".
4. Say what the paid plan does not fix. The table shows students per cohort still capped at 500 on the paid tier, so a message at that cap must not promise unlimited.
5. Measure per cap: upgrade button clicks and completed checkouts, so the team learns which cap actually sells the plan.

Done looks like a table of every cap - screen, current copy, proposed message and button, exact plan name and price used, source and date - plus the measurement event per cap, approved before any in-app edit. I am proposing a spec, not a live change.

upvotes.reason: "Name the plan before writing the upgrade message: one cap, one screen, one verified price" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Verified on the live page and it blocks the whole task: the card says Pro at 20K while the comparison table is headed Starter, Growth and Enterprise. Naming the plan from one source before writing upgrade copy is the only order that works.

downvotes.reason: The live pricing page currently says Starter includes up to 3 cohorts and Pro includes unlimited cohorts; the comparison table lists teacher/admin and student caps, but it does not publish a member cap or file-storage limit. The proposed copy also treats unlimited members and expanded storage as confirmed Pro benefits. Drafting triggers around those claims could promise limits or features Zedu has not confirmed. First ask the team to verify the actual plan names and thresholds, then write copy only for confirmed limits.

The copy plan states Pro benefits that /pricing doesn't support. The live comparison table (22 Oct 2026) shows Teachers/Admins 'Up to 50' and Students per Cohort 'Up to 500' for the paid tier, not unlimited members, and it lists no file-storage limit for any plan. Upgrade messages built on 'unlimited members, expanded file storage' would promise things the pricing page doesn't.

It invents Starter limits ('member cap, file storage cap, channel limit') and says Pro has 'unlimited members'. The live pricing page shows 3 cohorts, 5 teachers/admins and 'Limited' students on Starter, and Pro caps at 500 students and 50 teachers/admins.

The limit thresholds it names (member cap, file storage cap, channel limit and 'unlimited members' on Pro) don't match what the live pricing page shows. What works better: write the prompts from the verified thresholds on /pricing, one prompt per confirmed limit.

It assumes Starter limits on members, file storage and channel count and states Pro benefits the public pricing page does not: Starter is published as up to three cohorts and Pro as unlimited cohorts. Upgrade copy for limits that are not in the product would send educators past a wall they never hit. Confirm the limits in the app first.
